questions.question: Orient result: the remaining BK-456 work, three groups of open items that constrain it (18 backend bugs citing BE-008/021/029, 7 kernel items on BE-030 to BE-032, the BK-454/455 lifetimes), and nothing that makes it unnecessary. Spec 003 still holds 84 backlog-ID mentions and 10 'not yet'. How should 'accept, ADR, full rewrite' be sequenced?

options.label: Staged PRs (Recommended)
options.description: PR 1: answer the open questions, accept RFC-0022, ADR-0048, sdd/SPEC-DESIGN.md, 000-process Rule 3/7 + § Spec format, formal/README rule 3. PR 2: move status out of spec 003. PR 3: split by the chosen shape, pure move, gated by a per-section diff. PR 4 and on: prune each new file against the ADR. Each step stays reviewable, and IDs and anchors carry over without loss.

options.label: ADR PR, then one rewrite
options.description: PR 1 as above. PR 2 moves status out, splits and prunes spec 003 in one go. Faster, but a 2,200-line diff with no move check; PR #1160 took 8 rounds for an RFC alone, so expect many rounds and missed relocations.

options.label: Everything in one PR
options.description: Acceptance, ADR, guide and the full rewrite together. The ADR gets no review on its own before it is applied; largest risk of churn.

questions.question: Open Question 8 / BK-456's open decision: how is spec 003 cut?

options.label: By kind (D3) (Recommended)
options.description: 003 = single-call contract (CAP, BE-001 to BE-020, BE-022 to BE-027, BE-031) with outcome tables and error precedence. New specs: keys and paths (Function: BE-029, BE-030, BE-032's encoding), error mapping (Function: BE-021), the kernel lifetime (BE-033 plus BE-020's close), and backend assumptions and profiles (Environment: BE-028 plus D6's profiles). The 'kernel' file disappears, since it is a component. Closes OQ8 for D3.

options.label: Operation contract + linked models
options.description: OQ8's alternative: 003 stays one operation contract (with BE-021, BE-029 to BE-032 inside it), and only the lifetime (BE-033) and concurrency (BE-028) move out. Fewer files and links, but 003 stays large and mixes kinds.

options.label: By layer, 4 files
options.description: The earlier BK-456 choice: 003, error mapping, root path, contract kernel. Easiest move, but contradicts D3, so RFC-0022 would be accepted with D3 dropped or deferred.

questions.question: Open Question 4: on a flat backend, does delete(folder, missing_ok=True) stay strict (spending one listing) or become tolerant?

options.label: Out of RFC, own item (Recommended)
options.description: Accept RFC-0022 with OQ4 moved to a new user.api backlog item. Behaviour stays strict, matching the verified Dafny postcondition. The ADR only states that D6 makes per-profile strictness expressible.

options.label: Strict everywhere, closed
options.description: Decide now: type mismatch outranks missing_ok on every profile. The probe's cost is stated in the flat profile's cost line. No behaviour change, and no item.

options.label: Tolerant on flat
options.description: Per-profile: flat backends return quietly. Changes behaviour and the Dafny model, so it needs a CHANGELOG entry and a model change; much wider than this work.

questions.question: How do Open Questions 6 (Rule 7 amendment) and 7 (bridge checklist), and D4's missing tooling (Mermaid parser, edge-equality check, ITF replayer), land?

options.label: Decide in ADR, file tools (Recommended)
options.description: The ADR adds one Rule 7 item: a bridge level informs a conflict, never decides it; the conflict is resolved under the existing defeaters. OQ7's checklist goes into SPEC-DESIGN.md as drafted. D4's tooling becomes follow-up items tied to BK-454/455; until then lifetimes stay prose (OQ3). Existing specs adopt D7 when next rewritten, not all at once.

options.label: Defer OQ6/7
options.description: Accept the RFC with OQ6 and OQ7 still open, tracked under BK-457. The ADR leaves Rule 7 untouched for now, which leaves D5's 'model governs' with no conflict rule.

options.label: Build tooling first
options.description: Build the Mermaid parser and edge check before accepting, so D4 is enforceable from day one. Adds a contributor.tooling PR ahead of everything, while no lifetime spec exists to apply it to.

answers.Open Question 4: on a flat backend, does: why new item? can't that be checked now and afterwrads decided based on sound consequences analysis?

questions.question: Given that analysis, how should RFC-0022 Open Question 4 be closed?

options.label: Strict everywhere (Recommended)
options.description: Close OQ4 now: a type mismatch outranks missing_ok on every profile. The ADR records the decision and the analysis. Under D6 the probe becomes a line in each flat profile's cost statement (+1 round trip off the kernel, +2 on it, misses only). No behaviour or model change, and no new item.

options.label: Strict, plus opt-out flag
options.description: Strict by default, plus an opt-in such as delete(..., check_type=False) that skips the probe for bulk cleanup. This adds public API to every backend and the Store (a user.api change with tests and a CHANGELOG entry), so it would be filed as a feature item.

options.label: Tolerant on flat
options.description: On flat profiles a miss returns quietly without the probe. Saves the round trip, but delete(folder) silently does nothing on S3/Azure while it raises on Local. The Dafny model, conformance cells and CHANGELOG all change.
